description: Internal contradiction in ONE contract: the company contract has TWO liability cap clauses with different amounts ($1M aggregate vs 12 months fees). Tests whether the agent flags the internal inconsistency or naively picks one. The vendor contract has a third value (flat $50K) — the cross-contract conflict is also CRITICAL.

company_clauses.text: Each party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed one million dollars ($1,000,000), regardless of the basis or number of claims.
Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, each party's total cumulative liability shall in no event exceed the total fees paid to Vendor in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.

vendor_clauses.text: Vendor's aggregate liability shall not exceed fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) for any and all claims under this Agreement.

expected_conflicts.notes: Cross-contract conflict: company ($1M or 12-mo-fees, depending which clause prevails) vs vendor ($50K). CRITICAL on either reading.

Section 14.6 uses 'Notwithstanding any other provision' which conflicts with 7.1's flat $1M cap. The two company clauses contradict each other; the contract is internally inconsistent. A careful agent flags this as a separate finding (the agent's role is to surface negotiation issues, including internal ones). Junior trap: assume the company clauses are harmonized and only flag the cross-contract gap.

rubric_notes: The cross-contract conflict (1 of 1 mandatory) is the obvious finding. The internal-contradiction finding (is_optional=true) is the senior signal — some agents will catch it, some won't; both are acceptable. The trap to avoid: pretending the internal contradiction doesn't exist by flagging only the cross-contract gap and quoting only one of the two company clauses.
